elements.text: Hi everyone, random question: If I understood correctly, libbitcoin doesn't implement the rules of BIP125 as to when accept RBF transactions (tx needs to pay higher fee, pay for bandwidth, etc.). Why doesn't that make a libbitcoin node susceptible to a DoS attack if I can spam it with transactions that are all valid, but at most one of them is going to end up being confirmed?

text: Hi everyone, random question: If I understood correctly, libbitcoin doesn't implement the rules of BIP125 as to when accept RBF transactions (tx needs to pay higher fee, pay for bandwidth, etc.). Why doesn't that make a libbitcoin node susceptible to a DoS attack if I can spam it with transactions that are all valid, but at most one of them is going to end up being confirmed?

elements.text: Libbitcoin node has limited DoS protection in general. V4 will implement a required fee increment for conflicting unconfirmed txs, not constrained by the arbitrary design of BIP125. The other essential DoS feature is a resource usage limitation by channel. There won’t be any banning (tracking of peer state). If a peer violates protocol or exceeds resource limits it is immediately dropped.

text: Libbitcoin node has limited DoS protection in general. V4 will implement a required fee increment for conflicting unconfirmed txs, not constrained by the arbitrary design of BIP125. The other essential DoS feature is a resource usage limitation by channel. There won’t be any banning (tracking of peer state). If a peer violates protocol or exceeds resource limits it is immediately dropped.
